hints: On an x–t graph, velocity is the slope. What is the slope of a line at 30°, and at 60°?
worded:
1. Straight x–t lines mean constant velocities, each equal to the slope of its line.

2. Slope = tan of the angle with the time axis: tan 30° = 1/√3 and tan 60° = √3.

3. Ratio = (1/√3) : √3 = 1 : 3. (D)

4. Trap: the ratio of the angles (1 : 2, option A) means nothing; it’s the tangents that matter.
mistakes: Velocity is tan θ, not θ; 30° : 60° is not 1 : 2 in velocity.
Reading slopes as tan θ only works when both axes use the same scale; here the question intends that.
